investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state and the agent was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible to run peer-pod workloads. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable node exists for any new remote-agent pod. Because the pod never started, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned a VM ID or a remoteState value, leaving all four required evidence fields absent and causing the contract validation to fail entirely. This is a Kubernetes infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval infrastructure or code defect.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready']; neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible peer-pod nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving zero capacity for new remote-agent pods. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, meaning only 2 nodes are ever candidates. If those 2 nodes have reduced capacity (e.g., a node was cordoned, drained, or lost), effective schedulable capacity drops to zero. Supported by the '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' clause in failed-check.message.

Tertiary — peer-pod quota or limit configuration: a cluster-level or namespace-level ResourceQuota or LimitRange for kata.peerpods.io/vm may be set too low relative to current demand, causing the resource to appear exhausted even if physical capacity exists. Not directly evidenced but consistent with the scheduler message.

Out-of-scope hypothesis — eval runner or code defect: no evidence supports a runner bug; the runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1880-1885 is structurally correct and the failure message originates from the Kubernetes scheduler, not from application logic.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the failure, the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a different scheduling or API error would need to be identified.

If the pod spec for remote agents did not request kata.peerpods.io/vm as a resource, the scheduler message would not be attributable to resource exhaustion and a node affinity misconfiguration would become the primary cause.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeded and produced all four required evidence fields, the failure would be transient (e.g., a brief capacity spike) rather than a sustained exhaustion condition.
If only remote-agent-create failed while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime passed, a shared node capacity constraint would be disproved and a check-specific issue would need investigation.
If the eval runner's withCleanup wrapper is confirmed to have successfully deleted all prior remote-agent pods, leaked pod accumulation as a cause of capacity exhaustion would be ruled out.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries the Kubernetes API for available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity before attempting remote agent creation, and fails fast with a descriptive capacity-exhaustion message rather than waiting for pod scheduling timeout.

Add a cluster node capacity eval that independently monitors kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used across all nodes and alerts when headroom drops below a configurable threshold (e.g., fewer than 2 free slots).
Add a leaked-pod detection eval that lists all remote-agent pods older than a configurable TTL and flags any that were not cleaned up by the eval runner's withCleanup wrapper.

Consider adding a historical pass/fail trend eval for remote-agent-create so that the verifierContext.history fields (lastPassingAt, previousStatuses) are populated, enabling regression detection on future runs.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes have no available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector), causing every remote-agent pod to remain unscheduled for 133–144 seconds before the eval times out. Because no pod ever started, the runner could not collect any evidence, leaving all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) absent and triggering a full contract violation.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that label. The remaining four nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector, so preemption is also unavailable. This infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion prevents any remote-agent pod from being scheduled, which means the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) never returns a running agent, and the state-polling step that would produce orgId, agentId, readyState, and state evidence is never reached. This is an eval-observed infrastructure failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state and the agent was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible to run peer-pod workloads. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable node exists for any new remote-agent pod. Because the pod never started, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned a VM ID or a remoteState value, leaving all four required evidence fields absent and causing the contract validation to fail entirely. This is a Kubernetes infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval infrastructure or code defect.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler returned 'Unschedulable: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod was never scheduled.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=140742, status=fail, endedAt=2026-07-01T16:42:38.357Z — the check timed out waiting for a pod that never became schedulable.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was ever written, consistent with the agent never being created.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing, matching the contract defined at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error message, latencyMs=151350, no evidence collected — confirms the same node capacity constraint blocked a second independent pod.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error message, latencyMs=145241, no evidence collected — confirms a third independent pod was also blocked.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; this call never returned because the pod was unschedulable, so no evidence was written downstream.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready']; neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible peer-pod nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving zero capacity for new remote-agent pods. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, meaning only 2 nodes are ever candidates. If those 2 nodes have reduced capacity (e.g., a node was cordoned, drained, or lost), effective schedulable capacity drops to zero. Supported by the '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' clause in failed-check.message.

Tertiary — peer-pod quota or limit configuration: a cluster-level or namespace-level ResourceQuota or LimitRange for kata.peerpods.io/vm may be set too low relative to current demand, causing the resource to appear exhausted even if physical capacity exists. Not directly evidenced but consistent with the scheduler message.

Out-of-scope hypothesis — eval runner or code defect: no evidence supports a runner bug; the runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1880-1885 is structurally correct and the failure message originates from the Kubernetes scheduler, not from application logic.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the failure, the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a different scheduling or API error would need to be identified.

If the pod spec for remote agents did not request kata.peerpods.io/vm as a resource, the scheduler message would not be attributable to resource exhaustion and a node affinity misconfiguration would become the primary cause.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeded and produced all four required evidence fields, the failure would be transient (e.g., a brief capacity spike) rather than a sustained exhaustion condition.
If only remote-agent-create failed while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime passed, a shared node capacity constraint would be disproved and a check-specific issue would need investigation.
If the eval runner's withCleanup wrapper is confirmed to have successfully deleted all prior remote-agent pods, leaked pod accumulation as a cause of capacity exhaustion would be ruled out.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries the Kubernetes API for available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity before attempting remote agent creation, and fails fast with a descriptive capacity-exhaustion message rather than waiting for pod scheduling timeout.

Add a cluster node capacity eval that independently monitors kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used across all nodes and alerts when headroom drops below a configurable threshold (e.g., fewer than 2 free slots).
Add a leaked-pod detection eval that lists all remote-agent pods older than a configurable TTL and flags any that were not cleaned up by the eval runner's withCleanup wrapper.

Consider adding a historical pass/fail trend eval for remote-agent-create so that the verifierContext.history fields (lastPassingAt, previousStatuses) are populated, enabling regression detection on future runs.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes have no available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector), causing every remote-agent pod to remain unscheduled for 133–144 seconds before the eval times out. investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that label. The remaining four nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector, so preemption is also unavailable. This infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion prevents any remote-agent pod from being scheduled, which means the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) never returns a running agent, and the state-polling step that would produce orgId, agentId, readyState, and state evidence is never reached. This is an eval-observed infrastructure failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

If user-traffic or incident signals showed remote agents successfully provisioning for real users during the same window, the failure would be isolated to the eval probe's scheduling context (e.g., a dedicated eval namespace with tighter resource limits) rather than the shared production scheduling pool.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries the Kubernetes scheduler or node resource API to assert that at least one kata.peerpods.io/vm slot is available before attempting remote-agent pod creation — this would catch capacity exhaustion earlier and with a clearer signal than a pod-stuck timeout.

Add a dedicated eval for kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool health that independently verifies node label coverage and available VM resource capacity, decoupled from the end-to-end remote-agent-create flow.

Add a remote-agent pod scheduling latency eval that fails fast (e.g., within 30s) if a pod does not transition out of Pending, rather than waiting the full 133–144s currently observed, to reduce eval cycle time during infrastructure failures.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to help. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner never reached the agent creation or runtime call, so zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were collected and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state) is identical across all three sibling checks, confirming the failure is at the VM-slot scheduling layer, not in the eval runner logic or the expected-output contract definition. The eval infrastructure failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact is unconfirmed.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots exhausted on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: all three checks report the same Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm message, indicating the peer-pod VM quota is fully consumed and no slots are available for new agent pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remaining 4 nodes are structurally ineligible (wrong labels or taints) for remote-agent pods, meaning the effective scheduling pool is only 2 nodes, making exhaustion more likely under concurrent load.

Tertiary — concurrent or leaked agent pods consuming all VM slots: if prior eval runs or user workloads left agent pods running without cleanup, the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource would remain allocated, blocking new scheduling. The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (run-status-probes.mjs line 1916) is intended to prevent this, but a prior failed cleanup could leave orphaned pods.

Lower confidence — node affinity configuration drift: a change to node labels or pod affinity rules could have reduced the eligible node pool below what is needed, but no supporting config change is present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe on the 2 affinity-matching nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm slots available (not exhausted), the resource-exhaustion hypothesis is wrong and the cause lies elsewhere (e.g., a quota policy, admission webhook, or node-level runtime failure).

If the Unschedulable message disappears on a re-run without any cluster intervention, the failure was transient (e.g., a burst of concurrent pods that have since terminated) rather than a sustained resource exhaustion.
If a re-run with AURA_STATUS_CHECKS=remote-agent-runtime passes and returns all 5 required evidence fields, the cluster has recovered and the failure was self-healing.

If the 4 nodes with affinity mismatch are found to have been recently re-labeled or tainted (not reflected in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges), the root cause would shift to a node configuration change rather than VM slot exhaustion.

If orphaned pods from prior eval runs are not found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, the leaked-pod hypothesis is disproved and the cause is either genuine capacity exhaustion from user workloads or a quota reduction.
